title: The unions of Abba and Ima: Shabbos, Yom Tov and the week of the mind, up to the birth of souls
overview:
The last chapter showed three ways *chachma* and *bina* receive from the *Keser*: from the *mazalos*, where a person loves a thing for itself and so sees every detail; from the *zro'os*, where the intellect is the emotions' puppet; and from *Nehi*, where it is a tool for a goal it cannot question. This chapter shows the same range in *Abba* and *Ima* themselves.

Their inner union is *Shabbos* and *Yom Tov*, leisure for the mind. On *Shabbos* *chachma* rests and sees G-dliness as it is, before it is named; on *Yom Tov* *bina* enjoys the inner point, through symbols and *mitzvos*. Their outer side, the *middos* of the intellect, is the mind that leans to a verdict: felt without reasons in *Yisroel Saba*, like Rav who kept silent, and explained in *Tevuna*; and its *Nehi* weighs how to carry the verdict out, with conviction or without. The inner union is like a couple who simply enjoy each other; in the *Shema* it is reached by *mesirus nefesh*. Souls are born only from a union that reaches the *mazalos*, as only a great sage who knows an idea at its source can teach it to a child.

sections.title: The light goes down through Abba and Ima themselves: from the mazalos to the outer Nehi
sections.summary: Chapter 25 explained the ways *chachma* and *bina* receive from the *Keser*: from the *mazalos*, from the *zro'os*, or from *Nehi*. This chapter shows the whole range of *Abba* and *Ima* themselves, from their inner intellect that receives from *Arich* to their outer *Nehi* that goes into *Zeir Anpin*; and the level they receive from decides how true the intellect is.

blocks.text: The last chapter explained the ways *Chabad* (*chachma*, *bina* and *daas*) can receive from the *Keser* (crown): from the *mazalos* (lit. the flows; he compares them to hairs), which reach the *Chabad* of the *Keser* and up to its essence; from the *zro'os* (the arms), the *middos* (emotional attributes) of the *Keser*, its *vav* (six emotions) enclothed in the arms of *Arich Anpin*; or in the normal way, from the *Nehi* (*netzach*, *hod* and *yesod*) of *Arich Anpin*, since the *Nehi* of the higher goes into the lower.

blocks.text: This chapter explains three levels of the *yichud* (union) of *Abba* and *Ima*: *chachma* and *bina* as *partzufim* (statures), working together to understand an idea. They are *trein rei'in d'lo misparshin*, two companions that never part. As soon as an idea comes in *chachma*, you analyze, order and name it in *bina*; whenever you analyze in *bina*, you look in *chachma* for how it all fits together. When they come together to produce ideas, they can do it on three general levels.

blocks.text: "It seems to me," Rabbi Walters says, that these three levels of the union match the three sources of the last chapter: the level it receives from is the level of its union. The middle one, the *zro'os*, is "like a puppet": intellect blinded by emotion, "or like political things". Above that, it gets from the *mazalos*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 30 reads no line of the chapter: it is his introduction to the whole chapter, placed under its first line.

blocks.text: A review of the last chapter. If a person's desire is for the intellect itself, it comes from the *Chabad* of the *ratzon* (will): the *Chabad* is true and he pursues the true idea. If it comes from the emotions, the intellect is a puppet, used to justify them. From *Nehi*, it is a tool, a *merkava* (a vehicle for the will): objective, but only about the means to the goal the *ratzon* wants; the goal "is not up for discussion". That is normal everyday intellect. At your job you do not think, "Should I be doing this? Is this the right job for me?" You just think how to do the job.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 30 reads no line of the chapter: it is his introduction to the whole chapter, placed under its first line.

blocks.text: On *Shabbos* you are supposed to be on the level of the *mazalos*. Intellect from the *mazalos* has the inner *taanug* (delight) hidden in it, and it makes a person very smart. The *mazalos* are of the *Chabad* of *Arich Anpin*, the *mocha stima'a* (the hidden brain), but their root is in the liquid of the brain and higher, in the skull. So it really comes from the *middos* of *Atik*, enclothed in *Arich*: *pnimiyus Abba* (the inner side of *Abba*) is *pnimiyus Atik*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 30 reads no line of the chapter: it is his introduction to the whole chapter, placed under its first line.

blocks.text: That is why a person with a big talent for something is one whose intellect receives from the *mazalos* in it. He loves the thing itself, as an end in itself, so his intellect enjoys and looks at every detail. The more something becomes a means to an end, the less you care, and the more you look at it in a superficial, general way, passing over the details that would make you really good at it.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 30 reads no line of the chapter: it is his introduction to the whole chapter, placed under its first line.

blocks.text: That is why someone like the Rebbe would be very smart at everything, even naturally. It is true of us too: when you learn *Chassidus* and take it to heart, it makes you smart in everything, because "the thing that makes you stupid" is not paying attention to the details, looking over it generally, like a *girsa* (rote) thing.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 30 reads no line of the chapter: it is his introduction to the whole chapter, placed under its first line.

blocks.title: The kid with the hockey cards
blocks.text:
Most things in life a person sees as not very important, so he does not think about them. His teacher told him of a kid who was not so good at math, or at school in general, but had hockey cards and knew every statistic for every player, and could work out all the percentages, "because he loved it."

So if a person only enjoys the football, he goes through everything else on autopilot, doing the bare minimum, and he will not notice the details or really understand them.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 30 reads no line of the chapter: it is his introduction to the whole chapter, placed under its first line.

blocks.text: *Chassidus* teaches you to find the G-dliness in everything; that is *iyun* (close analysis). The *iyun* and *girsa* of the first chapter are really about how you go through the world: whether you stop to find the word of G-d, the *Elokus* (G-dliness), in things, or pass over it. When everything has *Elokus* in it, each thing is an end in itself, with essential value. You care about its little details and spend time on it, and that makes you very good at everything, especially when you see how they connect.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 30 reads no line of the chapter: it is his introduction to the whole chapter, placed under its first line.

blocks.text: That is the *mazalos*: your essential *taanug* goes into the thing, so you want the thing itself. And that is why they are like hairs: the *tzimtzum* (contraction) of a hair brings the whole essence over "in a tiny drop". So you see everything as a little example of G-dliness, *mamash* (actually) G-dliness: not a means to an end but the end itself, a *metzumtzam* (contracted) piece of the real goal. That makes a much bigger intellect, and a bigger *taanug* in it.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 30 reads no line of the chapter: it is his introduction to the whole chapter, placed under its first line.

blocks.text: If it is only the *zro'os*, the *middos* going into *chachma* and *bina*, he is like a very smart person who is always thinking into what he sees, but with an agenda: he uses everything to prove his view.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 30 reads no line of the chapter: it is his introduction to the whole chapter, placed under its first line.

blocks.title: Proving the Rebbe is Moshiach
blocks.text:
Say somebody is always trying to prove that the Rebbe is *Moshiach*. That is how he learns a *sicha* (talk), and really how he does everything. He does not appreciate the thing itself, its value or its lesson; he sees it as outside his point, and uses it.

He can use it as the puppet, or as a means to an end. A means to an end: since he wants to spread that the Rebbe is *Moshiach*, he learns publishing and radio so he can publicize it. "But he really doesn't care about it at all."

A means to an end can be unconnected to the essential thing, as when he is finding the best word to translate something about the Rebbe being *Moshiach*: nothing there can affect what he believes. The level of the *middos* is when he worries that something could.

blocks.title: Parents who overlook what their child did
blocks.text: So he feels threatened, and he has to twist it. Parents who love their child see him do something wrong, and often their intellect twists it to overlook it. A person does the same with himself: he sees himself a certain way, and when something he did contradicts it, he covers it up. That he is good, or his child is good, is already a given; this threatens it, so he has to wrestle with it. That is the level of the *middos*: the thing is not the essence but a symptom of it.

blocks.title: Driving to work
blocks.text:
There it has to fit the essential thing, and it is a threat if it does not. *Nehi* is not threatening. Figuring out how to drive to work, if you have to take a detour you do not care: "You just want to get there so you can get the money."

The intellect that decided you have to go to work is a bias of love for your family: you have to provide for them. How to get there is already cold; "I love them, so I have to provide for them" is hot. It is not the love itself, you could love them without going to work, but it is a sign: love them and not want to provide for them "doesn't look great."

blocks.text: Now: **now we have to understand the way the light goes down further, how it goes through the ten sefiros of Abba and Ima themselves**. The *mashal* (analogy) of *Abba* and *Ima* is a father and a mother.

This applies whenever the *Keser* goes into *chachma* and *bina*, but it is discussed *davka* (specifically) here, in *Atzilus*, because the *partzufim* (*Atik*, *Arich*, *Abba*, *Ima*, *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva*, five or six however you count them) are usually spoken of in *Atzilus*. Above *Atzilus* is before the *Tikun* (the world of Repair): there is no division of lights into vessels, ten into ten, so no *partzuf* yet, just the points of *Tohu*. The *Adam* of *Adam Kadmon* is a general *partzuf* for everything, not a particular one.

And they are not in *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, because there the *partzuf* is not real: it is only revealed in something separate. Those worlds are like thought, speech and action, separate from the essence.

blocks.title: The student in class and at recess
blocks.text: A *partzuf* is a person's ten powers used for a certain thing. Using all ten to learn is *Abba*: a learning personality. See a student in the classroom, then out at recess socializing, and "it could be a totally different thing." His hobbies and passions, what he enjoys, are an *Atik*-*Arich* *partzuf*. Dealing with him day to day, whether he is a nice guy, what you normally call his personality, is his *Zeir Anpin*. How good he is at speaking and doing, whether he is a charismatic speaker, is a *Nukva*. These are the conscious mind revealed in the body.

That is *Atzilus*: consciousness as it is revealed in the body. Above it is the subconscious. Below it, it comes out of you into expression, what you say or do: the *partzufim* are expressed there, "but it's not alive anymore." So plain *partzufim* are in *Atzilus*, the world of *Tikun*; that is why they are discussed here, and why chapter seven, at the start of the *hishtalshelus* (the chain of descent), puts them there. It applies elsewhere too, just differently.

It would not fit earlier or later, because there it is not what that level stresses. "The light" that goes down is the revelation of the person's self: how his self-expression comes down and stays transparent through the ten *sefiros* of *Abba*, the intellect.

blocks.text: **From the level of the pnimiyus of the intellect of chachma and bina**: the inner side of the *mochin* (lit. brains, the intellect) receives from **chesed and gevura of Arich Anpin**, and even more inner, **when they receive from the mazalos of Arich Anpin**. That is rare, not even normal intellect, which is the emotions and then the *Nehi*. "Most people like barely even tap into the *mazalos*."

Most people, even when they do philosophy, are only on the level of the *middos*. They are not pursuing the truth so much as emotionally defending their world view, which is why they get emotional when they discuss it: they feel the conclusions threaten how they live, or their view of themselves as good. The very fact that they come at it to reach a conclusion one way or the other shows they are on the level of the *middos*.

*Chassidus* does not tell you good or bad about anything. It tells you what it is, very clearly, and how everything fits together. That is why it lets you find the good in everything, in a detached way. "The real question is when to use which one, not which one is true."

Then there are people with a real *chush* (sense) for something, geniuses at it, passionately into it, enjoying every little detail like a real artist. That is a *mazalos* guy: the thing, with its details, is an end in itself. To be like that with philosophy he has to love truth, love understanding the way things are, not to reach conclusions but as a *lishma* thing, like pure science. Even applying it, he does it to see how it is when applied, still not as a means to an end.
The real *mazalos* thing is *Chassidus*; "that's what *Chassidus* is." Even the other levels of Torah are not really like the *mazalos*, which is why they are *halacha* (law) and such things.

blocks.text: So the range runs from the *mazalos* **all the way down to when only the external Nehi of Abba and Ima**, enclothed in the *mochin* of *Zeir Anpin*, give, as in *Etz Chaim*. You want to see how *Abba* and *Ima* go all the way up and all the way down: "the whole spectrum of *Abba* and *Ima*'s *Abba*-and-*Ima*-ness." The last chapter was the ways the *Keser* can give to *Abba* and *Ima*; this one is the levels of *Abba* and *Ima* themselves, from receiving from the *mazalos* to giving into *Zeir Anpin*.

sections.title: Shabbos and Yom Tov: the inner union of chachma and bina, for its own sake
sections.summary: The inner *mochin* of *Abba* and *Ima* are like *Shabbos* and *Yom Tov*, leisure for the mind. *Shabbos* is called *kodesh* and *oneg*: *chachma* resting, seeing G-dliness as it is, as an end in itself; *Yom Tov* is only *mikra kodesh* and *simcha*: *bina* enjoying the inner point of the idea, through symbols and *mitzvos*. Where the two meet, *havein b'chachma v'chacham b'vina*, is the inner union of *Abba* and *Ima*.

blocks.text: **And the inyan is known, that it's like Shabbos and Yom Tov.** They are a *mashal* for the inner intellect of *Abba*, **because Shabbos is called holy**, *kodesh*, and *chachma milsa b'garmei*: **chachma is a thing onto its own**, an end in itself. *Kodesh* means removed from everything else, needing nothing: the pleasure is in it itself. So *Shabbos* is *kodesh b'oneg*, holy in delight.

*Shabbos* is when you rest your *chachma*. The difference between work and leisure is not so much what you are doing but whether you want to be doing it, whether you enjoy it as an end in itself, so you would do it even without the money. Work is what you would rather not do, but you need the money.

*Shabbos* and *Yom Tov* are leisure: *Shabbos* the rest of *chachma*, *Yom Tov* the rest of *bina*. On *Shabbos* you have fun with *chachma*; on *Yom Tov* your *bina* has fun. *Shabbos* is the inner side of *chachma*, an end in itself; using *chachma* to figure out right, wrong and how to act is its outer side, for the week.

On *Shabbos* your *chachma*, your creative ability, gets a break from figuring out how to make money, and even from figuring out *halachos*, to do what it likes: see G-dliness in things in a pure way, pure science, not applied. Applications are work for it.

During the week the mentality is that things are bad and you have to be *mevarer* them (sort them out): *b'chachma isbariru*, with *chachma* you sort out how to act. But then nothing is really G-dliness: you want to sit and learn *Chassidus* in yeshiva, and you have to learn law, do business, even eat and sleep. Most days are a drag. *Shabbos* is a whole different *hisbonenus* (contemplation).

On *Shabbos* you look for the actual G-dliness in everything, *b'chol derachecha da'eihu* (know Him in all your ways). Nothing needs fixing: G-d made it, so it has His wisdom in it, and you look for that. That is why on *Shabbos* you enjoy the taste of food, not only its energy as in the week: how He chose to make it taste is also a revelation of His wisdom. And it is a *mitzva* (commandment) to do it on *Shabbos*.

blocks.title: Playing the game and watching the video
blocks.text:
During the week the *mitzva* is to be *mevarer* the world. Playing a basketball game, you do not say, "It's just a game." You care, try hard, and do not give the other guy a free shot because he messed up; that ruins the game. When it is over and you are watching the video, you enjoy even your mess-ups, and are not "all competitive and a sore sport."

G-d has both. Six days you play the game. On *Shabbos* you rest and enjoy the beauty, like a vacation, thinking about Torah, and even your *hisbonenus* is not sorting out your *middos* but appreciating that everything is *Elokus*.

blocks.text: **This is the pnimiyus of the or Abba**, the inner side of the light of *chachma*: the inner desire in *chachma*, the pleasure of thinking about something you really enjoy, here G-dliness. A person is revealed mainly when he uses his *chachma* in something he loves; the main light is there. The person does not become the *chachma*, but this is the inner side of its light, when it receives from the *mazalos*. It shows what he enjoys. Outer *chachma* shows only the *chachma*: "you don't see what he's choosing."

That is the difference between the *mitzvos* and the world. The world is like outer *chachma*: you see G-d's wisdom, how He chose to make it, but not what He chose to represent Himself and connect Himself to. That is the *mitzvos*.

The inner side of *Abba* is the inner side of *Atik*: **so that's the pnimiyus of Atik Yomin**, the inner pleasure. So *v'karasa laShabbos oneg*, **you should call Shabbos pleasure, or that you should bring pleasure into Shabbos**, because the *taanug* is revealed in the *chachma*. **As explained elsewhere at length about the three seudos** (meals) **of Shabbos**: for *Chakal Tapuchin Kadishin* (the field of holy apples), *Atik Yomin* and *Zeir Anpin*. "I don't know much how it's connected."

blocks.text: **And Yom Tov is called not kodesh, it's only called mikra kodesh** (a calling of holiness): only its spreading forth, a lower level. On *Shabbos* the *chachma* goes up; on *Yom Tov* only the *bina* does, and the *chachma* is still working. That is why on *Yom Tov* you may do *borer* (sorting) for *ochel nefesh* (preparing food), and on *Shabbos* not.

*Yom Tov* is analyzing the world to understand it: not seeing G-dliness in its purest state, but understanding it in human intellect. That brings the idea down to the world: you take things from it to compare, make *meshalim* (analogies), order it, see it in examples. That is *ochel nefesh*: you make food from the world "to feed the G-dliness." You see the G-dliness indirectly, come down from its essential state; that is *bina*.

*Yom Tov* also has a *chumra* (stringency) over *Shabbos*: *nolad* (a thing newly come into being) is *muktza* (not to be handled) on *Yom Tov* and not on *Shabbos*. *Yom Tov* is analyzing what you already have, not dealing with new information, *chiddushim* (new insights); that is work for *bina*. *Shabbos* is *chachma*, whose essence is coming up with new things.

*Yom Tov* is a lot more fun than *Shabbos*, but not as restful. You can carry your *sefarim* and make food; "it's easier to party on *Yom Tov*." But on *Shabbos* you cannot do anything, so you do not worry about anything, not even making food. "The way it is, that's the way it is, and you just enjoy it."

*Yom Tov* is *mikra kodesh*, **which is simcha** (joy). *Oneg* (delight) is the revelation of *kodesh* directly, so *Shabbos* is called *oneg*; *Yom Tov* is its spreading forth into your *yeshus* (sense of self), which is *simcha*. As chapter four said, *chachma* makes *bittul* (self-nullification) and *bina* makes *simcha*. In *chachma* the pleasure is from the thing, so you lose your *metzius* (existence) and feel the thing. *Simcha* is understanding it in your own vessels: you have it, "you're on top, you're the boss," and since it is very big, the *simcha* is big.

That is *mikra kodesh*, **like it says, the mother of the children rejoices**: *bina* associates something with something outside it. *Mikra* is calling, giving it a name: you connect to the essence, but artificially. It is not yet applying it, which would be the week; you are finding ways to represent it, so it is no longer the thing itself. That is human intellect: symbols, names, systems and order that represent the idea. So it is *mikra'ei kodesh*: you call it *kodesh*, but it is not essentially *kodesh*.

So *Yom Tov* has *mitzvos* you have to do, and *Shabbos* has none: "you just sit there and do nothing." On *Yom Tov* we express our connection to G-dliness; on *Shabbos* it is essential and needs nothing to show it. You do not even have to make *kiddush*: "The *mitzva d'oraisa* is not to say *kiddush*, it's to enjoy things, to have wine." The *mitzva* is to appreciate that G-d made the world and rested, that everything has that G-dliness, and you say it to be conscious of it, to be *mekadesh* the day. There are good food, nice clothes, a nice table, but no real *mitzvos* of the day.

On *Yom Tov* you have wine either way: no *simcha* without wine. Once it must come a certain way, you have said, this is how we represent it, and "it's out of your hands a little bit already."

blocks.text: *Chachma* says, "Just be yourself, man. We accept you as you are." So with the world: the point of *Shabbos* is to stop trying to change things and enjoy the world as it is. G-d made it perfect; you do not have to do anything. No rules, except do not spoil the fun: do not ruin the vacation by thinking about work. "That's the only rule here: you have to have fun."

On *Yom Tov* you have already decided to have fun by playing a certain game, and you play by the rules: we show our connection to G-d through *matza* and *sukka*. But these are general *mitzvos* that show our essential connection and *emuna* (faith). *Matza*, flat and tasteless, shows the *emuna* and represents the *chachma*. The *sukka* shows that Torah and *mitzvos* are not an end in themselves but a temporary thing that we see through: we just want to connect to G-d. The *Yamim Tovim* reconnect us to see that the week's *mitzvos* are between the *chachma*, *Shabbos*, and the week, an expression of the *chachma*. That is *bina*.

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת מוחין דאימא שמקבל מאבא,
phrases.en: which this is the *mochin* of *Ima*, the intellect of *bina*, which receives from *chachma*.

phrases.he: כי השביתה דשבת הוא בחכמה גם כן
phrases.en: the resting of *Shabbos* is in *chachma*,

phrases.he: דהיינו בפנימית אבא, בחינת כח מה אין דחכמה
phrases.en: which that is the inner part of *chachma*, the *koach MaH*, which is the *ayin* of *chachma*,

phrases.he: קודם שמתפשט ליש בהשגה דבינה
phrases.en: even before it comes into be understood in *bina*.

blocks.text: *Em habanim semeicha*, **which this is the mochin of Ima, the intellect of bina, which receives from chachma**. **The resting of Shabbos is in chachma**: in **the koach MaH** (the power of "what"), **which is the ayin of chachma**, its *ayin* (nothing), **even before it comes into be understood in bina**. On *Shabbos* it is revealed: you take things in as they are, before you interpret and name.

blocks.title: Drawing on the Right Side of the Brain
blocks.text:
*Drawing on the Right Side of the Brain*: "It's a very good book," about drawing, and a very good book about *chachma* and *bina*. Its whole point is to put you into *chachma* mode, and that is the secret of drawing: look at the thing exactly as it is, instead of naming its parts and drawing the parts you named.

Looking at a face, a person sees eyes, nose, ears, mouth, glasses, and draws a symbol for each, so it looks like symbols for a person. What you actually see, depending on the angle, may look nothing like the symbol. So you train yourself to draw what you see, lines and shadows, lights and darks, without naming it. And most details have no names, so when you name things you leave those out, and it does not look right.

Looking at it as it is, without naming and categorizing, it stays whole. Naming it picks what you consider important, which is why *Atik* is revealed in *bina*: what you care about shows in the distinctions you make. It is like the blot test: the *chachma* is an uninterpreted blob, and the interpretation comes from you, since you could cut it up and name it differently. You find what you look for. So it is a way of looking into the person; that is how *bina* reveals the *Atik*, what he really enjoys.

phrases.he: וכן בינה בבחינת פנימית,
phrases.en: and the same thing that on *Yom Tov*, which is the *pnimiyus* of *bina*,

phrases.he: הוא עומק נקודת המושג כו',
phrases.en: that's the *omek nekudas hamusag* of *bina*.

phrases.he: כידוע שיש אין חכמה בבינה ובינה בחכמה
phrases.en: that there is the *ayin* of *chachma* goes into *bina*, and the inner thing of *bina* is in *chachma*.

blocks.text: **And the same thing that on Yom Tov, which is the pnimiyus of bina**: **that's the omek nekudas hamusag** (the depth of the point of the concept) **of bina**. On *Yom Tov* you focus on the inner point of the idea, not the proofs, examples or applications. That is the resting of *bina*, which enjoys the inner point; so on *Yom Tov* we focus on the inner point of the *mitzvos* and of sorting out the world, the goal.

blocks.title: The object of the game
blocks.text: The object of the game: in *bina* it is to win by getting the most points. In *chachma* it is just to have fun, and you can have fun even if you do not win; *chachma* can have fun doing anything. In *bina* fun takes a certain form: it is fun to win. So on *Yom Tov* you do not do a lot of work, "it's not practice time," but you still do some, because you have to win the game.

It is known **that there is the ayin of chachma goes into bina, and the inner thing of bina is in chachma**: at their inner points they connect. Analyzing anything, you analyze the thing itself, so there is always *chachma* in it; and even getting the *chachma*, you notice details and interpret a little, to see how it differs from other things, so there is always *bina*. "You can't really have one without the other."

phrases.he: והיינו הבן בחכמה וחכם בבינה,
phrases.en: that in the *chachma* itself, you'll be able to find the ability to make the distinctions and then explain it, and from the explanations, you'll be able to get the inner point, which is the *chachma*.

phrases.he: שזהו בחינת יחוד פנימית דאבא ואמא
phrases.en: That's the inner *yichud* of *Abba* and *Ima*, *chachma* and *bina*,

blocks.text: That is *havein b'chachma v'chacham b'vina* (understand with wisdom and be wise with understanding): **that in the chachma itself, you'll be able to find the ability to make the distinctions and then explain it, and from the explanations, you'll be able to get the inner point**. **That's the inner yichud of Abba and Ima**, working together just for the inner truth of an idea; it comes from the *mazalos*.

blocks.title: Three levels of a marriage
blocks.text: The simple *mashal* is a father and a mother. A married couple relates on three general levels. One is spending time together because they enjoy it, for no other purpose: the relationship is an end in itself. That is the inner union of *Abba* and *Ima*, the mental connection and the enjoyment of each other. The man has to come down to recognize the *bina*, the woman to recognize the *chachma*, and the love is expressed in small symbolic things, "like flowers and little notes." But it is for themselves, not like raising kids together, doing the taxes, taking out the garbage or washing the dishes.

blocks.title: Stuck in traffic, and raising kids
blocks.text:
Those can also be done with *pnimiyus*, as a chance to spend time together. Stuck in traffic: "Oh, it's an opportunity we get to spend time. Who cares?" *Nehi* mode is, "Man, I got to get there quick."

In between is raising kids. There is a level where they connect higher than the kids: the inner side. The middle, regular thing is that the purpose of marriage is to make a family and raise children. Then there are work and taxes, the practical things of living together: not the purpose, a means to keep the house going, with money and food.

sections.title: The outer flow: the middos of chachma and bina, intellect that leans
sections.summary: When *chachma* and *bina* flow outward into their *Chagas* and *Nehi*, the intellect is a means to an end. The *middos* of *chachma*, its *vav ketzavos*, are the mind applied to a case or leaning toward kindness or judgment; they shine into the *middos* of *bina*, which give them good reasons, before they are born as emotions of their own.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן בחיצונית השפע דחכמה ובינה בחג''ת נה''י כו',
phrases.en: On the other hand, when the *chitzoniyus hashpaa* is going into *Chagas* and *Nehi*

phrases.he: כמו מדות שבחכמה
phrases.en: Like the *middos* of *chachma*

phrases.he: שנקרא בחינת ו׳ קצוות דאבא
phrases.en: which are called the six directions, the six dimensions of *Abba*

blocks.text: **On the other hand, when the chitzoniyus hashpaa** (the outer flow) **is going into Chagas** (*chesed*, *gevura* and *tiferes*) **and Nehi**, it is a means to an end, not an end in itself: **like the middos of chachma, which are called the six directions, the six dimensions of Abba**, the *vav ketzavos*. That is *chachma* expressed within time and space, in a particular form: its expression, circumstantial, not the thing itself.

blocks.title: The law and the case
blocks.text: You learn a *halacha* as an abstract law. An actual case comes within certain circumstances of time and space: that is the *vav*. Applying the law to the case is *chachma* going into its six directions. A precedent is the opposite: you extrapolate the *chachma* from the particular case.

phrases.he: כמו חסד שבחכמה,
phrases.en: Like *chesed sheb'chachma*,

phrases.he: דהיינו כח שכל המטה כלפי חסד
phrases.en: like that you can use the intellect to lean towards *chesed*,

phrases.he: או כח שכל אחר שמטה כלפי דין כו'
phrases.en: or you have another *koach* of the *sechel* to go towards *din*.

blocks.text: And *middos*: **like chesed sheb'chachma** (kindness within wisdom), **that you can use the intellect to lean towards chesed, or you have another koach** (power) **of the sechel** (intellect) **to go towards din** (judgment). So you can use intellect to prove emotions. But the real thing of intellect is to understand how things are; using the facts to prove your views is using it for your own benefit.

phrases.he: ומאירים בחסד וגבורה דבינה
phrases.en: And the *chachma* shines into the *bina*, so the *middos* of *chachma* shine into the *middos* of the *bina*,

phrases.he: דהוא בא בהשגה בטוב טעם בהסבר לזכות ולחוב
phrases.en: So, in *bina*, it becomes very well explained, good reasoning for whether for merit or for guilt.

phrases.he: ונקרא מדות שבשכל המושג,
phrases.en: These are called the *middos*, the emotions of the intellect, which is understood,

phrases.he: קודם שנולדו במהות בפני עצמן (כמו שיתבאר)
phrases.en: before the *middos* become actual their own thing, before they become just *middos* without intellect, which is *Zeir Anpin*, like we'll explain later

blocks.text: **And the chachma shines into the bina, so the middos of chachma shine into the middos of the bina**, which come up with explanations to make it sound rational: the point that supports the *midda*, why he thinks it is good or bad. Sometimes a person has such a point but cannot explain it, because his *bina* is not so good. "Doesn't mean it's not true"; some people are just better at arguing.

**So, in bina, it becomes very well explained, good reasoning for whether for merit or for guilt.** **These are called the middos, the emotions of the intellect, which is understood, before the middos become actual their own thing**, *middos* without intellect, which is *Zeir Anpin*, whose birth is explained later.

sections.title: Shatik Rav: silence is a fence for wisdom
sections.summary: When a person sees that a thing is so and cannot explain it, that is the *middos* of *chachma* before they shine into *bina*, like Rav who kept silent. Silence protects a *chachma* from being argued away, and it keeps the mind open to the source of all ideas, so that being quiet "gets you double".

phrases.he: וכאשר אינו מוצא טעם בהסבר השגה,
phrases.en: and when you do not find a reason, that you can't explain it,

phrases.he: ומכל מקום לא יוכל לומר בהיפוך
phrases.en: but you still can't say the opposite.

phrases.he: כי שכלו מטה כך,
phrases.en: because his intellect leans that way.

phrases.he: היינו בבחינת חסד וגבורה דאבא קודם שמאיר מאין ליש בבינה
phrases.en: That is the emotions of *chachma* before they shine into *bina*.

phrases.he: (כמו ענין שתיק רב כו')
phrases.en: like it says about *shatik Rav*,

blocks.text: **And when you do not find a reason, that you can't explain it, but you still can't say the opposite**: you see it is true but cannot explain it. Not everybody is good at explaining. "I feel that it's wrong." Why? "I don't know, I just see that it's wrong." **Because his intellect leans that way.** **That is the emotions of chachma before they shine into bina**, **like it says about shatik Rav** (Rav was silent).

blocks.title: Rav was silent
blocks.text: The *Gemara* in *Beitza* about *nolad*, an egg laid on *Yom Tov*, says *shatik Rav*. Some distinction kept one *halacha* from being learned from the other, but he could not find it. So he was quiet: he did not retract his ruling or argue further, and another sage explained it. That is the *mashal* for *Yisroel Saba* (lit. Israel the elder), the *middos* of *chachma*.

phrases.he: (והשתיקה סייג לחכמה,
phrases.en: a fence for the wisdom

phrases.he: משתוקא בתרין,
phrases.en: being quiet gets you double.

phrases.he: מפני שעולה ביטול כח מ''ה דחכמה זה למקור המוציא כל השכלות,
phrases.en: this *bittul* of the *koach MaH* of *chachma*, where you just experience it as it is, without interpreting it, you're able to go to the source of all the intellect,

phrases.he: שנקרא חכמה סתימאה כנזכר לעיל,
ומוציא משם השכלה חדשה כו')
phrases.en: and you can get out a new idea

blocks.text: *Ushtika seyag l'chachma*: silence is a fence that protects the *chachma*. The simple meaning, in *Pirkei Avos*, is that if you sit and listen you learn a lot, and once you open your mouth you stop learning. But why call that **a fence for the wisdom**? A fence protects something you already have. So he explains it further: when you have a *chachma* and give no reason for it, that protects it. Once you give a reason, it is open to be argued with and disproven.

blocks.title: The Rebbe's advice for a debate on TV
blocks.text:
The Rebbe told, he thinks, Rabbi Hollander, who was asked to debate Judaism with a Reform rabbi on TV and did not want to give him credence as a legitimate rabbi, to say first thing: "I do not agree with your stance at all, and I do not recognize you as a rabbi. Now, let's discuss the issues."

He starts with the premise, not open for debate, axiomatic, that you are not a legitimate rabbi, "and it's not Judaism. You're Jewish because you were born Jewish, but this whole ideology has nothing to do with Judaism." If you want, I can try to prove it, but even if I fail, that is not up for debate. That is one way silence is a fence for wisdom.

sensitivity.reason: Says of the Reform movement and of a Reform rabbi that he is not a legitimate rabbi and that his religion is not Judaism, in a story about a named rabbi told from memory.

blocks.text: Also, when you are trying to get an idea you are quiet: in the *chachma* you see the thing itself, and interpreting it disturbs that. You have to let it in as it is. That is why a person with a flash of an idea goes quiet.

*Mishtuka b'trei* (silence is worth two). "Maybe you have a name for this in Latin": in *halacha*, sometimes a person makes a claim and gets $100, where if he had kept quiet he would have got $200, because his claim impairs his rights. By opening his mouth he got one; quiet, he would have got two. **Being quiet gets you double.**

Here it means the *bittul*, the silence, gives you a better understanding. *Chassidus* does not interpret anything; it understands as it is, and that is the difference between G-dly and human intellect. Being quiet that way gives you double. With **this bittul of the koach MaH of chachma, where you just experience it as it is, without interpreting it**, you get it objectively, so **you're able to go to the source of all the intellect**, the hidden *chachma*, **and you can get out a new idea**, since you did not put it in a box. Attach it to a reason and you limit it: if the reason is disproven, the whole thing looks bad, and you can hardly make a *chiddush* outside that context.

sections.title: Netzach and hod of Abba: the scales of the mind and the strength of conviction
sections.summary: The *Nehi* of *Abba* is the scales of the intellect, the *kelayos yo'atzos* that weigh how a verdict should be carried out. *Netzach* and *hod* are the mind's legs: a person who is *takif b'daito* stands by his view, and one who is not falls easily from guilt to innocence. Only from the *Nehi* of *Abba* in the *Nehi* of *Ima* come the *mochin* of *Zeir Anpin*.

phrases.he: ובחינת נה''י דאבא, היינו בחינת מאזני השכל והחכמה, איך שיבא הדבר חכמה לידי השפעה בבחינת כליות יועצות כו'

blocks.text: *Nehi* of *Abba* is the scales of the intellect: how the *chachma* comes to be given over. Once the intellect has decided whether a thing is good or bad, you have to figure out how to apply it, like the difference between the verdict and the sentence. *Chachma*, *bina*, *chesed* and *gevura* are the verdict, still abstract. Then: what are we going to do about it? The scales weigh how it should come out.

That is the *kelayos yo'atzos*, the kidneys that give advice. When it comes to doing it, should you go at it gung-ho, or timid, with restraint? *Netzach* wants the full thing, good or bad, "the full extent of the law." *Hod* holds back a little, because that would be better, or because you are scared it will be too much.

blocks.title: The lashes and the first offender
blocks.text:
Deciding how many lashes to give a man, *netzach* wants to give him all of them; *hod* is scared you will kill him. The purpose is that he should live and be better, so you are careful not to give too much and ruin his chance.

So in court, a first offender, especially a young one, is often not thrown in jail; they want him reformed, not rotting away there, "that's not productive." If he keeps doing it, "they throw the book at him." Those are the kidneys that give advice.

phrases.he: (והיינו ענין התוקף שיש במוח, שנקרא תקיף בדעתו
phrases.en: This is also the force of your views, when you are strong-minded, when you're strong in your opinions, in your views.

phrases.he: כמו הרגלים
phrases.en: like the legs

phrases.he: שיש בהן כח להקים כל הגוף,
phrases.en: they have the strength to hold up the whole body.

phrases.he: כך בחינת נצח והוד דאבא מקימין לגוף המוחין
phrases.en: so too *netzach* and *hod* of the *chachma* hold up the actual intellect.

phrases.he: ולהיפוך
phrases.en: and the opposite,

phrases.he: כשאינו תקיף בדעתו,
phrases.en: a person is not strong-minded,

phrases.he: בקל יפול מסברתו מחוב לזכות
phrases.en: he can easily fall from his reasoning from guilt to innocence,

phrases.he: ומטמא לטהור כו'
phrases.en: impure to pure,

phrases.he: וכן בנצח והוד דאמא)
phrases.en: and the same thing with the *netzach* and *hod* of *Ima*.

blocks.text: This is *takif b'daito* (firm in his mind): **the force of your views, when you are strong-minded**. **Like the legs, they have the strength to hold up the whole body, so too netzach and hod of the chachma hold up the actual intellect.** Otherwise **he can easily fall from his reasoning from guilt to innocence**; **and the same thing with the netzach and hod of Ima**.
Without a strong *netzach* and *hod*, even though they are only the outer side of the intellect, you will not have the guts to seal it one way, because you can always argue the other side.

That is liberalism, or pluralism: they do not have the strength in their view, the conviction, to stand up (the *mashal* of the legs, "following all these English correspondences") for what they believe in, take a stance and say, "That's it, this is it, and you are wrong, and therefore we..."

sensitivity.reason: Names liberalism and pluralism as views whose holders lack conviction, a political jab.
sensitivity.publishable: That is a person without the strength in his view, the conviction, to stand up (the *mashal* of the legs, "following all these English correspondences") for what he believes in, take a stance and say, "That's it, this is it, and you are wrong, and therefore we..."

blocks.text: To have a legal system, by the way, you have to feel strongly enough that this is right and that is wrong to take responsibility for punishing somebody. That strength of opinion comes mainly from *netzach* and *hod*. In theory the different sides have truth, but when it comes to doing it, one way is best; and even if it is not the best, doing it one way matters more than finding more possible ways.

So for a proactive, task-oriented person, it does not matter so much whether the system is the best. "It's better to have a system and a leader" that you follow and get things done than to sit around working out the best system; in theory you can always improve it, but you will never get anything done. That is why *Elul* is the time to stop and make a *cheshbon hanefesh* (an accounting of the soul). The rest of the year you focus on doing, not second-guessing yourself.

phrases.he: ודרך כלל, הרי רק מבחינת נה''י דאבא שמלובשים בנה''י דאימא, משם נמצא מקור המוחין לזעיר אנפין, שהן בחינת המדות שלמטה מן השכל (כמו שיתבאר)

blocks.text: In general, only the *Nehi* of *Abba* enclothed in the *Nehi* of *Ima* is the source of the *mochin* of *Zeir Anpin*, the *middos* below the intellect. Once you have a *midda*, an intellect says how and when to have it. Day to day you are not thinking about the meaning of life and your goals; you figured out your priorities once, and from them what to like and what to hate. Now that is an *uvchein* (a conclusion), and your intellect is just how to react to what goes on around you.

blocks.title: The job and the family
blocks.text:
A person has *ahava rabba* (great love) in the *Chagas* of his will: he loves his family, so his intellect makes him get a job to support them. On the job, the *Nehi* of the will goes into the *Nehi* of the intellect: he has to do the job well, not think about his family the whole time. That practical intellect becomes the *mochin* for the *middos*: happy to make a profit, scared to lose money.

It comes from the *Nehi* of *Abba* going into the *Nehi* of *Ima*. A gut feeling of how to do things is the *Nehi* of *chachma*. In the *Nehi* of *Ima* he understands it a little and explains to himself when to have the *midda* and when not, and then he has the *middos*. This comes later, with how the *middos* of *Zeir Anpin* are born from the intellect.

sections.title: Two unions: for their own sake and for new mochin; Shabbos, the Shema and mesirus nefesh
sections.summary: *Abba* and *Ima* unite either in their inner side, for themselves, like a couple who simply enjoy each other, or in *Nehi* alone, to give new *mochin* to *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva*, like workers calling a manager. That is the difference between *Shabbos* and the week. In the *Shema*, *Havaya Elokeinu* is the inner union and *Havaya Echad* the union below it; it is reached by *mesirus nefesh*, as the ten martyrs raised *MaN* to the inner side of *Abba*.

phrases.he: וידוע פרטי עניני יחודים דאבא ואמא
phrases.en: Now we're going to explain the *pratei yichudim* of *Abba* and *Ima*,

blocks.text: **Now we're going to explain the pratei yichudim** (the particular unions) **of Abba and Ima.** *Abba* and *Ima* have three main levels. Their *Chabad* is like *Shabbos* and *Yom Tov*; their *Chagas* is like the inner side of the week, and their *Nehi* the regular week. The last two are the verdict and the sentence: is this good or bad, and what should you do about it.

phrases.he: בין כשהוא בבחינת הפנימית לצורך עצמן,
phrases.en: whether it's a *yichud* in the *pnimiyus* for themselves,

phrases.he: שהוא בבחינת ג׳ ראשין שבהן
phrases.en: which is the *gimmel rishonos*, the *Chabad* or the *Keser*, *chachma*, *bina* of the *mochin*,

phrases.he: קודם שמתפשטים במדות עדיין כו',
phrases.en: before it goes into the *middos*,

phrases.he: ובין כשמתייחדים לצורך מוחין חדשים לזעיר אנפין ונוקבה,
phrases.en: whether getting together to make new *mochin* for the *middos*

phrases.he: שהוא בבחינת נה''י לבד כו'
phrases.en: which is just the *Nehi*,

blocks.text: **Whether it's a yichud in the pnimiyus for themselves**, like *Shabbos* and *Yom Tov*, **which is the gimmel rishonos** (the first three), **the Chabad or the Keser, chachma, bina of the mochin, before it goes into the middos**: *chachma* and *bina* come together just to understand the idea, not yet to apply it. The *mashal* is a father and mother, who are also husband and wife, with a relationship that precedes their being parents: spending time together, talking, going out to eat. There is a reason, but none outside the relationship; it is for themselves, not yet for the *middos*.

blocks.title: Calling the manager
blocks.text: Or **whether getting together to make new mochin for the middos**, for *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva*. "You know what? We got to call a manager here, we got a problem." The *middos* run on autopilot on their instructions, but sometimes they hit a problem and need new *mochin*, so you call a manager who has brains; "the regular workers don't have brains, they just follow policy." The union that brings out new *mochin* for *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva*, how the emotions and thought, speech and action should be *b'poel mamash* (in actual practice), **which is just the Nehi**, is the outer side of the union.

phrases.he: וזהו ההפרש בין שבת לחול כו'
phrases.en: this is the difference between *Shabbos* and *chol*.

blocks.text: **This is the difference between Shabbos and chol** (the weekday). On *Shabbos* you focus on the essential connection of *chachma* and *bina*: learning just to know G-d, not to figure out how to act, like learning Torah *lishma* (for its own sake). Learning *halacha l'maaseh* (law for practice) is not what is called *lishma*; knowing the *halachos* in order to act is a separate *mitzva* from learning Torah, which is to know G-d's wisdom as an end in itself.

So too your *hisbonenus* in *davenen* (prayer) is not supposed to be an attempt to change your *middos*. It is appreciating G-dliness for its own sake: *avoda* of the mind, not for *birur* (refinement), not even of your mind, *lada'as Havaya levad*, just to know G-d. That is *Shabbos*. During the week the focus is refining your *middos*: learning *halacha l'maaseh*, and contemplating *Chassidus* to come out with something practical in *avoda*. Those are the two unions of the mind: learning a thing for itself, or to apply it.

phrases.he: (ובקריאת שמע הכוונה ביהו״ה אלהינ״ו, היינו בפנימית דאבא ואמא,
שמשם יהו״ה אחד,
phrases.en: as a result of that, *Havaya Echad*,

phrases.he: יחוד דזעיר אנפין ונוקבא
phrases.en: which is the idea of the *yichud* of *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva*.

phrases.he: כשבא להם בחינת תוספת מוחין חדשים
phrases.en: When they get this new *mochin*,

phrases.he: כדי שיוכלו להוליד כו'
phrases.en: so they can give birth.

blocks.text: In *Krias Shema*, *Havaya Elokeinu* is the inner side of *Abba*: *Havaya* is *chachma*, *Elokeinu* is *bina*, their inner union. Your *kavana* (intention) is that everything in the world reveals G-d, as an end in itself: He is our G-d, everything has a G-dly essence, and we are essentially connected to Him without having to do anything; we only reveal the connection. *Elokim* normally means nature and limitations, but here *Havaya*, higher than all limitations and above reason, chose that our nature should be connected to Him.

Just *Elokeinu* would mean we have to work to get it. *Chachma* is the thing as it is from the essence; *bina* is the way it is associated with something, as in a language. *Havaya* is the revelation of G-d, and *Elokeinu* means He made our nature a vessel to reveal Him. That we are a vessel we do not work for or deserve; that too comes from *Havaya*. "The Jew's connection to G-d is unconditional," above reason. "The nature of a Jew is that he's G-dly, that's it." It depends on nothing and is a means to nothing. "That is complete statement."

In *Shema Yisroel Havaya Elokeinu* you realize that *Havaya*, higher than nature, is our G-d. Learning the *hishtalshelus* you really only see it in you, the way he explains it in you, not in the world. Once you find G-d in you, it tells you *Havaya Echad*: He is in everything else the same way, by extension. Once you know the *nimshal* (what an analogy stands for) in you, how the *hishtalshelus* works in you, you know how it works in everything. As the Arizal says, one who knows how to make *yichudim* can know whatever he wants to know.

So *Havaya Elokeinu* is the inner side of *Abba*: not applying it, just appreciating that you are connected to G-d, as an end in itself. **As a result of that, Havaya Echad, which is the idea of the yichud of Zeir Anpin and Nukva**: G-d is one with the world and controls everything, the *middos* coming into *Malchus*, *hashgacha pratis* (Divine providence over every detail). But first you have to realize that G-d creates the world, that there is nothing else, so everything is by His choice and reveals Him. That changes your *middos* and how you see the world run: if every moment is recreated by His choice, everything is *hashgacha pratis*, everything has a lesson, and nothing can stop you from doing what G-d wants.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 36 opens in the middle of line 31, which tape 35 began; this continues it.

blocks.text: That new *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva* comes **when they get this new mochin**. Your *middos* are the way they are, and the world seems limited (to make money you have to do it this way), because your *mochin* are messed up: you think *teva* (nature) is a set thing. Once you realize that G-d recreates the world every moment, automatically you are scared of nothing but G-d and not *nispa'el* (overawed); you see the world differently. **So they can give birth.**

phrases.he: והיינו במסירת נפש דקריאת שמע,
phrases.en: And this is accomplished in the *mesirus nefesh* of *Krias Shema*.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן בתורה ומצות בלא מסירת נפש
phrases.en: when a person does Torah and *mitzvos* without *mesirus nefesh*,

phrases.he: אין היחוד רק בחיצוניות דאבא ואמא בזעיר אנפין ונוקבה, כמו שכתוב במקום אחר

blocks.text: **And this is accomplished in the mesirus nefesh** (self-sacrifice) **of Krias Shema.** With *mesirus nefesh* a person reveals his essential connection to G-d, based on nothing, not for any particular of Torah and *mitzvos*, and he can apply it to change his *middos*.

That is *Rosh Hashana* and *Yom Kippur*, and then *Sukkos*. Their *teshuva* (return) reveals this *mesirus nefesh*: a connection to G-d higher than Torah and *mitzvos*, that "you don't care about the Torah and *mitzvos*, you just care about G-d." Once you realize that, you do Torah and *mitzvos* with *mesirus nefesh*, from this essential connection, which is the whole reality of you and the world. Nothing can stop you revealing it or separate you, so nothing scares or overawes you, and then you do Torah and *mitzvos* properly.

blocks.title: A child cannot yet have children
blocks.text: You need a new worldview. Before, you were trapped by a false one, and that inhibition limited your *middos* and deeds and made you a *baal middos*. It is like a child who cannot have children until he gets *tosefes mochin* (added intellect), until he matures enough to have the *daas* for it. To give to someone outside himself, he has to feel his essence, be conscious of it, and not worry that he will lose it.

That is the *mesirus nefesh* of *Krias Shema*. But **when a person does Torah and mitzvos without mesirus nefesh**, he does not reveal G-d's essence. In a way he is not really doing a *mitzva*, only its external action, not from the inner side of the *mochin*, dedicated to something higher. It is how he was trained: he still believes what he always did and still serves himself, and thinks "the best chance of them getting lollipops is if they listen to their mommy and *tatty*." It is *mitzvas anashim melumada* (a commandment of men, learned by rote), within his nature, not really for G-d.

So it does not change him; he is still within his limitations. And in return G-d does not do miracles for him or change nature for him, since he lives in the false reality of nature and believes in it. But one who realizes the world is an arena for Torah and *mitzvos* that cannot stop him, that becomes his nature. A *shliach* (emissary) of the Rebbe who goes in the Rebbe's powers and does what the Rebbe tells him finds it normal that everything works out: "So then miracles happen all the time." It is *midda k'neged midda* (measure for measure).

phrases.he: וכמו בענין עשרה הרוגי מלוכה
phrases.en: like the ten martyrs

phrases.he: שהעלו מיין נוקבין לאבא ואמא בבחינת הפנימית על ידי מסירת נפש דוקא)
phrases.en: they made a *ha'ala'as MaN* to *pnimiyus* of *Abba*

blocks.text: **Like the ten martyrs**, whom we read about on *Yom Kippur* soon: through *mesirus nefesh* davka **they made a ha'ala'as MaN** (a raising of *mayin nukvin*, the receiver's arousal from below) **to pnimiyus of Abba** enough to sustain the worlds until *Moshiach*. G-d's pleasure in it made the whole thing worth doing "just for them." *Mesirus nefesh* serves no purpose, not even Torah and *mitzvos*; it shows the essential connection, and revealing that is the main thing of the world. They revealed the *yechida* (the essence of the soul).

blocks.title: The interested students
blocks.text: It is like any relationship, a teacher and students, a husband and wife. If students put in effort and show big interest, that is a *ha'ala'as MaN*: you feel they really want it, and you want to give more. It works both ways: when a husband feels his wife is dedicated to him and appreciates him, he is motivated to give more and be more.

*Mesirus nefesh*, selfless dedication, reveals the essential connection higher than anything: he gives himself over to you, as with *naaseh* before *nishma*. Our commitment is the *MaN* to G-d; His commitment to us is the drawing down of *MaD* (*mayin duchrin*, the giver's flow). There is commitment to the *mitzvos*, and *mesirus nefesh* to G-d, in a way higher than the *mitzvos*. The martyrs gave their bodies and gained nothing; it was only to show they are for G-d: "if G-d wants me to die, so I'll be willing to die, that's it," even tortured to death.

blocks.title: The chassid willing to give his life
blocks.text: There is dedication to a subject, and dedication to you. A teacher gives far more when students will listen to whatever he says and give up everything for him. Imagine a *chassid* of the Rebbe willing to give his life away: that is a big *ha'ala'as MaN*.

blocks.title: The Holocaust and Moshiach's delay
blocks.text: The Holocaust was in a way even more: often they had no choice, and it was everybody. The story where they sing *Ani Maamin* is "just crazy *ha'ala'as MaN*." "I don't really understand how it's possible to have that kind of stuff happening with *Moshiach* not coming, cuz it's so disproportionate. It's like this huge *ha'ala'as MaN* that's like ridiculous, and then what comes from it?"

sections.title: Upper and lower Abba and Ima: Yisroel Saba and Tevuna, and the mazalos that give souls
sections.summary: The union of the upper *Abba* and *Ima* is the couple as husband and wife; the lower, *Yisroel Saba* and *Tevuna*, is them as father and mother, the intellect as it is revealed outward, felt in *Yisroel Saba* and explained in *Tevuna*. To give *mochin* to *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva* for the birth of souls, the union must reach up to the two *mazalos* of *Arich*: a soul needs the essence of the intellect, not yet set in a form.

phrases.he: (וזהו ענין יחוד אבא ואמא עילאין ויחוד אבא ואמא תתאין,
phrases.en: and this is the idea of the upper union of *Abba* and *Ima*, and the lower union of *Abba* and *Ima*.

phrases.he: שהוא ישראל סבא ותבונה, כמו שכתוב למעלה בענין בינה ותבונה באריכות
ובחינת ישראל סבא הוא ו׳ קצוות דאבא ותבונה ו׳ קצוות דאימא

blocks.text: **This is the idea of the upper union of Abba and Ima, and the lower union of Abba and Ima.** The upper is *Abba* and *Ima*; the lower is *Yisroel Saba* and *Tevuna*, the six directions of *Abba* and of *Ima*, as was explained at length about *bina* and *tevuna*. "So the upper is the, wait, what is he going to say?"

phrases.he: ויש עוד ישראל סבא למעלה גם מאבא ואמא עילאין
שהוא ו׳ קצוות דחכמה סתימאה דאריך אנפין
ותבונה ו׳ קצוות דבינה דאריך אנפין
שמשם נמשך שורש יחוד אבא ואמא עלאין בבחינת ג׳ ראשין שבהן כו')

blocks.text: There is also a *Yisroel Saba* above the upper *Abba* and *Ima*, the six directions of the hidden *chachma* of *Arich Anpin*, and a *Tevuna*, those of its *bina*; from there is the root of the upper union in the *gimmel reishin* (three heads). So *chachma* and *bina* can unite in their pure state, for their own revelation, not for the children. Father and mother as husband and wife are the upper union; as father and mother, the lower, *Yisroel Saba* and *Tevuna*. In the *mashal*, *Abba* and *Ima* are the parents' personality, their *mochin* and *middos*; *Yisroel Saba* and *Tevuna* are like the reproductive organs, the physical father-and-mother part: the *middos* of the *chachma* revealed outward.

But there is a *Yisroel Saba* and *Tevuna* higher still, in *Arich*, above the upper *Abba* and *Ima*, and the root of their union comes from there. A really smart person, who has the essence of the intellect, can explain it to a little kid; that comes soon. Chapter two explained *bina* and *tevuna*.

*Yisroel Saba* and *chachma* differ the same way: applied intellect and pure intellect. *Tevuna* is the *middos* of *bina* revealed outward, what the intellect dictates about good or bad and how to do it: like learning *Shulchan Aruch* as opposed to *Gemara*, where even the *halacha* is hidden in the pure abstract thing, "the way that we learn *Gemara*, at least." *Yisroel Saba* and *Tevuna* differ only in whether you can explain it. When Rav knew the *halacha* but could not explain why, he just felt it: that is *Yisroel Saba*.

Normally pure intellect is higher than application. But there is a higher will, a higher level of application, in a way above pure intellect: the real thing of the Torah is doing the *mitzvos*, and its essence comes out when you apply it, do it and experience it. That is what made you want to understand even its pure side: that itself is a *mitzva*, and even the highest things should come out in some way as applied.

blocks.title: Parents and the will for children
blocks.text: Even if not in a particular way, an attitude of wanting to be connected to G-d, *lishma*, is the spirit of the law, and it lets you get the letter right. So with parents: they have an essential relationship that precedes having kids and is in a way higher, but they married mainly to make a family, and that will brought them together. "It's not just like they're friends." The strong, essential will for children is what makes the love between husband and wife so strong, since it is not essential in itself, as between a father and son. It starts off *talui b'davar* (dependent on a thing), and then is revealed as essential.
So the six directions of *Abba* are the intuitive halachic thing: you cannot explain it, but you have a *daas Torah* (a Torah sense), a *chush*, a feeling.

phrases.he: והנה כאשר נמשך מאבא ואמא מוחין לזעיר אנפין ונוקבה בשביל תולדות הנשמות,
phrases.en: when *Abba* is giving brains to *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva* in order to give birth to souls,

phrases.he: צריך להיות היחוד באבא ואמא בפנימית המוחין, בשרשם בב' מזלות דאריך אנפין
phrases.en: then there has to go to the *pnimiyus* of *Abba*, all the way up to the two *mazalos*.

phrases.he: (והיינו בני כו' במזלא תליה כו')
phrases.en: To have children and also *chayei u'mezonei* depends on the *mazal*.

blocks.text: **When Abba is giving brains to Zeir Anpin and Nukva in order to give birth to souls**, the union has to be in the inner *mochin*, at their root in the two *mazalos* of *Arich Anpin*: **then there has to go to the pnimiyus of Abba, all the way up to the two mazalos**. As explained elsewhere, *banei, chayei u'mezonei b'mazla talya*: **to have children and also chayei u'mezonei** (life and sustenance) **depends on the mazal**. You have to connect to the *mazal*.

For it to be a soul, a living thing that can change, you have to get the essence of the intellect. To *paskenen* (rule on) *halacha* it is not enough to learn *halacha*, "and the Gra says this": you have to know *pnimiyus haTorah* (the inner Torah), *Abba* in its essence. You have to know the real goal, G-d and what He likes, the spirit of the law. "Just tell me what to do and I'll do it" is not good enough, because there will always be gray areas, unless you appreciate what the Torah is on a level not directly connected to deed.

Otherwise it is not a soul but an angel, which does what it is told, like a machine, and cannot choose. To give birth to souls, with free choice and the ability to do things creatively, the inner *mochin* have to be revealed: G-d puts a *chelek* (portion) of His essence in. A *neshama* (soul) comes from the inner side of *Abba*, the level of the *mazal*, not yet limited in a form, which would set it one way. So souls reveal how G-d transcends every limitation, and have free choice; they are at the level of the essence.

blocks.title: The liquid over the brain, and stem cells
blocks.text: So with the physical making of a baby: some of the liquid over the brain comes down, the hidden *mochin*, the essence of life before it takes a particular form, "kind of like things like stem cells": not defined, so they can turn into anything. To have a child you bring out what in you is the undefined essence of life, so it can be made into something new.

sections.title: Kel Elyon and the great sage who can teach a child: why souls are born from above the intellect
sections.summary: *Kel Elyon* is the inner light of *Abba* going up to the *mazal*; from there *yesod* gives good kindnesses and "acquires everything". The *mashal*: only a *chacham muflag* who knows an idea at its source can explain it to a little child or bring out a new idea from it. So too souls are born only from a union of *Abba* and *Ima* that reaches above the source of their intellect, to the *mazalos*; and that is why it is on the night of *Shabbos*.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב במקום אחר
שזהו ענין אל עליון,
phrases.en: this idea of *Kel Elyon*, the upper force, the upper power.

phrases.he: עליית אור פנימית אבא כשמקבל ממזל ונוצר כו'
phrases.en: That is when the light of *Abba*, the *pnimiyus* light of *Abba*, receives from the *mazal v'notzer*.

blocks.text: This is *Kel Elyon*: **the upper force, the upper power**. *Kel* is a name of G-d and means power. *Kel* is the light of *chachma*, and *Kel Elyon* is the inner light of *Abba* rising to its source, receiving from the *mazal v'notzer*, from the *mocha stima'a*.

phrases.he: אז גומל חסדים טובים,
phrases.en: then it's able to give over good kindnesses,

phrases.he: בבחינת יסוד
phrases.en: in a way of *yesod*,

phrases.he: שנקרא קונה הכל,
phrases.en: which is called, acquires everything,

phrases.he: להוליד תולדות בזעיר אנפין ונוקבה
phrases.en: to give birth in *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva*.

blocks.text: **Then it's able to give over good kindnesses, in a way of yesod** (the attribute of relationship), **which is called, acquires everything**, *koneh hakol*, **to give birth in Zeir Anpin and Nukva**. Feeling the real essence of the intellect, you aim at the truth, and what you do is really *tovim*: *tov* is actually helpful, while *chesed* is being nice, and "you can mean well and not really be helpful."

*Koneh hakol*: you can acquire, have something separate connected to you and revealing you; here, children, your essence coming across into someone separate. For that you have to reach above the way you are revealed consciously in your body, to a level of your soul that could have gone into a different body, to different parents, made different choices, "and it would've been you, too." At that level anything can connect to it; "it's all yours." So a child, really a separate person, can be called yours, because there your essence *mamash* went into him.

phrases.he: וזהו וזוכר חסדי אבות ומביא גואל לבני בניהם כו'
phrases.en: And this is what it means that He remembers the kindness of the fathers and brings redemption to the children's children.

blocks.text: **And this is what it means that He remembers the kindness of the fathers and brings redemption to the children's children.** Going up to the source of the intellect, the source of the *avos* (fathers), He brings *geula* (redemption): the inner soul, to the children and children's children. *Gevura* is how it comes out in the vessel, the *mochin*, limited and set; the *chasdei avos* (kindness of the fathers) is its connection to the source, unlimited, able to come out any way. At that level it brings *geula* to the *b'nei b'neihem*: their children are the *middos*, their children's children the deed.

blocks.text: **The mashal of this is known**: a *chacham muflag* (a wondrous sage), **a really, really, really smart guy**. **If you want to teach it to a really stupid, low person, you have to really understand it well**; **then he can explain it even to a little kid**, **in a way that's totally different than the normal natural way that it's explained, which is very abstract and difficult**. **He can also come up with new sechel from it**: he has the essence, not limited to its form.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן מי שאינו חכם מופלג
phrases.en: somebody that is not a wondrous *chacham*, he doesn't get the *etzem* of it that's higher than it,

phrases.he: ואינו תופס רק החכמה והשכל דברים כהוויתן לבד
phrases.en: He only understands it as it is, what was explained to him.

phrases.he: די להפקיע להשיגו לעצמו בלבד
phrases.en: So, for him, it's enough that he's able to understand it for himself,

phrases.he: אבל לא יוכל להוליד חדשות ממנו כלל
phrases.en: he's not able to get anything new from it,

phrases.he: וכל שכן שלא יוכל להוליד ולהשפיל הסבר השכל להבינו לתינוק כו'
phrases.en: For sure he can't explain to a child,

phrases.he: ונמצא שבחינת נה''י דחכמה, שהוא בחינת יסוד, הכח המשפיע למקבל,
phrases.en: so it comes out the *Nehi* of the *chachma*, which is the *yesod*, the power of being *mashpia*, of teacher, the ability to be a teacher to a student,

phrases.he: תלוי בכח המשכיל, מקור חוצב השכל
phrases.en: depends on the *koach hamaskil*, which is the source of the intellect,

phrases.he: מאין ליש דוקא כו'
phrases.en: which brings it from its abstract essence to like a tangible form,

blocks.text: Whereas **somebody that is not a wondrous chacham, he doesn't get the etzem** (essence) **of it that's higher than it**. **He only understands it as it is, what was explained to him**. **So, for him, it's enough that he's able to understand it for himself**, but **he's not able to get anything new from it**: he sees it only in its current form and cannot find the essence and apply it to other forms. **For sure he can't explain to a child**: he cannot make a *chiddush* even in the abstract realm, and a little child is "totally irrelevant," so low; for him it is essentially abstract and academic.

**So it comes out the Nehi of the chachma, which is the yesod, the power of being mashpia** (the giver), the ability to be a teacher to a student, **depends on the koach hamaskil** (the power of insight), **which is the source of the intellect**, bringing it **from its abstract essence to like a tangible form**. There it is abstract and can come into any form, so one who taps into it can explain it even to a little kid.
That is why, if you want to understand *Chassidus* well, the best thing is to teach it. "It's very important. Just learning it, you're never going to understand it well, you have to teach it."

phrases.he: וכך הוא בענין תולדות הנשמות
phrases.en: same thing with this birth of souls,

phrases.he: מבחינת נה''י
שאינו מוליד כי אם בתוספת כח במקור המוחין שלו מלמעלה מעלה מן השכל כו'
phrases.en: In order for the souls to come out from the *mochin*, spiritually, it has to reveal the *etzem* that's higher than the *sechel*.

phrases.he: והוא הטעם שבשביל תולדות נשמות על ידי יחוד אבא ואמא,
צריך להיות מלמעלה ממקור המוחין דאבא ואמא
phrases.en: That's why it has to go higher than the source of the *mochin* of *Abba*,

phrases.he: שזהו מבחינת מזלות דחכמה סתימאה שהוא למעלה גם מחכמה ובינה דאריך אנפין עצמו כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: the *mazalos* are higher even than the *chachma* and *bina* of *Arich Anpin*, because the *mazalos* go all the way up to the *Keser*, all the way to the *etzem*.

blocks.text: **Same thing with this birth of souls**: **in order for the souls to come out from the mochin, spiritually, it has to reveal the etzem that's higher than the sechel**, so **it has to go higher than the source of the mochin of Abba**. And the other way around: for G-d to do miracles, to change things, we need *mesirus nefesh*. That is the *mazalos*, and **the mazalos are higher even than the chachma and bina of Arich Anpin, because the mazalos go all the way up to the Keser, all the way to the etzem**.

phrases.he: והיינו טעם ליחוד פנימית דאבא ואמא בליל שבת קודש
phrases.en: this is why the *pnimiyus yichud* of *Abba* is the night of *Shabbos Kodesh*,

phrases.he: מפני שהוא בשביל להוליד נשמות
phrases.en: because it's in order to bring down souls,

phrases.he: שלכך אז דוקא זמן זיווגא דחכימין
phrases.en: and that's why *talmidei chachamim*, their time when they have relations is *davka* on *Shabbos*,

phrases.he: שהן תלמידי חכמים שנקרא קודש,
phrases.en: because *talmidei chachamim* are called *kodesh*,

phrases.he: ושבת שרשו בקודש העליון,
phrases.en: and *Shabbos*, its source is in the *kodesh elyon*,

phrases.he: בחינת פנימית אור אבא כנזכר לעיל ודי למבין:
phrases.en: which is the *pnimiyus* of *Abba*, which receives from the *Keser*.

blocks.text: **This is why the pnimiyus yichud of Abba is the night of Shabbos Kodesh, because it's in order to bring down souls.** **And that's why talmidei chachamim** (Torah scholars), **their time when they have relations is davka on Shabbos**, *zivuga d'chakimin*: **because talmidei chachamim are called kodesh, and Shabbos, its source is in the kodesh elyon** (the higher holiness). Since they focus on the inner side of *Abba*, learning Torah *lishma* and appreciating the essential connection to G-d, they do it on *Shabbos*, the time of that thing.

reviewQuestions.question: Why does a person whose intellect receives from the *mazalos* become good at a thing, and what do the hockey cards show?
Why is *Shabbos* called *kodesh* and *oneg*, but *Yom Tov* only *mikra kodesh* and *simcha*?
What does *Drawing on the Right Side of the Brain* teach about the *koach MaH* of *chachma*, and how does naming reveal *Atik* in *bina*?
In what two ways is silence a fence for wisdom, and why does being quiet "get you double"?
How do *netzach* and *hod* of *Abba* hold up the intellect, and what do the lashes and the first offender show?
Why can only a *chacham muflag* explain an idea to a little child, and what does that show about the birth of souls?
